get.description:
Counters since start-up: requests, LLM calls, tokens against the daily cap and the monthly
allowance, how often narratives and analyst replies fell back, and replay sockets.

get.description:
The turning-point verdict under a preset (`style`) or custom sliders (all four), with the flip
reason measured against `vs` (the reference preset by default).

The template at once (status `pending` while a verified narrative is generated), or the cached
verified narrative. 404 for an unflagged possession or an unknown preset.

post.description:
Ask the analyst about a match. It answers from the engine tools over MCP, writes no numbers and
cites the possessions it talks about; status `offline` when no LLM is available.

get.description:
The team's top flagged moments for half-time (`half`: first-half moments) or full-time, grouped
into themes, each with its narrative and how the other presets would judge it. Narratives not ready
within about forty seconds come back as templates (status `pending`).

One event per flagged moment under a preset (the reference by default), for broadcast graphics:
when it happened, the chosen and best options, and a fan caption in every supported language. Serves
cached verified captions or templates; never starts LLM work.

AnalystReply.title: AnalystReply
AnalystReply.description:
The analyst writes no numbers: it cites possessions, and the UI shows their numbers from the engine.
Status: `verified`, `fallback` (a canned line with the moments found, after the verifier rejected the
answer twice) or `offline` (no LLM, or the daily allowance is used up).

Claim.title: Claim
Claim.description:
What a narrative asserts, checked against the engine: `better_option` names the best option under the
style (`ref` is its option ID), `chosen_fits_style` says the choice was the best one, `turning_point`
names the decision (`ref` is its index) and `style_principle` a factor on the style's card.

Latency.title: Latency
Latency.description: Over the most recent samples (up to 500); null before the first.

LlmMetrics.title: LlmMetrics
LlmMetrics.description:
Every model call, each step of a tool-calling loop included. The month's figures come from the token
ledger (null without a database); the cost is an estimate at Mistral Small 4 prices, against the monthly
included allowance.

MetricsReport.title: MetricsReport
MetricsReport.description: The API's own counters since start-up, for monitoring alongside Railway's CPU and memory graphs.

Narrative.title: Narrative
Narrative.description:
`template` holds {fact.id} slots and `facts` holds their values for this style and language; the
client fills the slots from `facts` alone, so no number in a narrative ever comes from the LLM.
Status: `template` (no generation planned), `pending` (template shown, generation queued), `verified`
(LLM text that passed the verifier) or `failed` (template shown, generation gave up).

OutcomeMetrics.title: OutcomeMetrics
OutcomeMetrics.description:
LLM-written outputs since start-up. `fallback`: a template or canned line was served instead, after
the verifier rejected the draft twice or the LLM call failed. `rejected`: outputs where the verifier
rejected at least one draft, retried or not. Rates are null before the first output.

PositionsChunk.title: PositionsChunk
PositionsChunk.description: Samples at a fixed rate. Each row is [x, y] per entity in `pids` order (ball first), flattened.

RuleSet.title: RuleSet
RuleSet.description: One side of a style: its slider positions and the principles behind them.

SliderSpec.title: SliderSpec
SliderSpec.description:
What one slider does: weights[f] += gains[f] * (slider - 0.5). Each factor has at most one slider, so a
flip attributed to a factor names the slider behind it.

StyleConfig.title: StyleConfig
StyleConfig.description:
Option score = sum(weights[f] * option.factors[f]); linear so any verdict change can be attributed.
Weights are derived from the sliders by the StyleLens.

StyleLens.title: StyleLens
StyleLens.description:
Everything needed to build any style from sliders, as the API does: weights = base + the sum over
sliders of gains * (slider - 0.5). Presets are rule-set pairs; flip reasons are measured against the
reference.

StyleShift.title: StyleShift
StyleShift.description:
How many of the pack's moments another preset judges differently, and the factor behind most of
those flips.
